free-tier flash models this app defaults to do genuinely return "model
overloaded, try again later" at busy times, and with no retry that surfaced
straight to the user after a long wait instead of quietly trying the
next-best available model the way screenshot import already does.

Added callGeminiText to working-with.js — a text-only sibling of the
existing callGeminiVision, same overload-detection and ranked-fallback-model
chain, just without an image attached — and pointed the AI fact route at it
instead of its own one-shot implementation.

entries.summary: Fix the sidebar commit hash too — same root cause as the changelog
entries.details:
The version readout's short commit hash used the same live `git rev-parse`
approach the changelog did before v3.5.1 — broken for the same reason
(no .git, no git binary in the production image), so it's almost certainly
been silently blank in Portainer this whole time regardless of how the
image actually gets built.

generate-changelog.js now also stamps the commit hash into changelog.json
alongside the entries, and server.js reads it from there instead of
attempting git at runtime. Same one-commit lag as the changelog entries
already have, for the same unavoidable reason (a commit can't know its own
hash before it exists) — negligible for what's fundamentally a "does this
look like a recent deploy" sanity check.

entries.summary: Fix changelog showing empty in production
entries.details:
The Docker image has no .git directory and no git binary at all (Alpine's
node:18 image doesn't ship one), so last push's runtime `git log` call for
the changelog silently failed every time in the actual deployment — hence
"No changelog available" in Portainer even though the sidebar commit hash
readout (which has the same problem, just less visibly) was probably also
blank.

Switched to a generated changelog.json, committed alongside every version
bump via scripts/generate-changelog.js and copied into the image like any
other static file — same fix as the Dockerfile's existing "explicit COPY
per server dir" pattern, just for a new file instead of a new directory.

entries.summary: Add a What's New changelog, read live from git history
entries.details:
Click the version number in the sidebar footer (rather than adding it as
its own nav row) to open a changelog: every "vX.Y.Z: summary" commit,
newest first, expandable for the full detail. A new /api/changelog route
parses this straight out of git log at startup (same pattern as the
existing commit-hash readout), so it can never drift out of sync with
what actually shipped and needs no hand-maintained list.

entries.summary: Fix duplicate colleague-in counts, stale re-imports, hardcode NFC/iCal URL, add Team Calendar search
entries.details:
- Who's In and the Dashboard's "Next In" card were missing the
  store-filter every other colleague query uses, so a colleague working
  at a different store today could show as "in" twice — once for their
  real (different-store) shift, once phantom. Both now correctly exclude
  non-home-store shifts.
- Re-importing a corrected team screenshot only ever added/updated rows —
  a colleague who'd been wrongly imported onto a day and is genuinely
  absent from the corrected screenshot stayed stuck in the database
  forever. Imports now reconcile: any home-store shift from a *previous*
  import that isn't represented anywhere in the new screenshot for a day
  it covers gets removed. Scoped to previously-imported rows only (never
  touches manually-added shifts) and to home-store data only (never
  touches a different store's shifts this screenshot has no authority
  over).
- The NFC clock-in tag URL and the calendar subscription link both used
  window.location.origin, so they'd bake in whatever local address you
  were on when you opened the page instead of the public domain. Added
  a "Public URL" field in Settings → General; both now use it when set.
- Team Calendar gets a search box — searches every shift ever imported by
  name/date/time/store in one go (reusing the same data the CSV export
  already pulls), with an Edit button on each result wired straight into
  the existing edit-shift modal. No more paging week by week to find one
  mistyped time.

entries.summary: Add an AI Bonus Fact to Did You Know
entries.details:
A first, deliberately small step towards using the app's existing Gemini
integration for more than screenshot import. A new "🤖 Ask Gemini for a
fact" button sends a compact, names-free summary of career stats (total
hours, pay, streaks, colleagues worked with, etc. — numbers only, no
shift dates or raw records) and asks for one fresh comparison-style fact,
in the same spirit as the hand-written facts above it but with room to
vary the angle each time instead of one fixed formula per fact.

On-demand only (a button click, not on page load) and single-attempt (no
retry/fallback-model chain like the screenshot importer has) — deliberately
minimal until it's clear this is worth building further, e.g. into a proper
"ask about my shifts" Q&A.

entries.summary: Collapse V2.0 sidebar group into a hub, like V3.0
entries.details:
Same treatment the V3.0 group got in v3.4.2: the eight V2.0 views (Synergy
Score, Team Metrics, Fatigue Audit, Shift Heatmap, Weather, What If?,
Streaks & Badges, Rota Wrapped) are now reached through a single "🚀 V2.0
Features" sidebar link to a card-grid hub, instead of an expandable group.
Each of the eight pages gets a back-to-hub button at the top, matching the
V3.0 pages.

entries.summary: Fix Shift DNA always landing on The Chameleon
entries.details:
The variety trait counted exact-minute distinct start times, but real rota
data has natural clock-in noise (06:45/06:48/07:02 for what's really one
"opening" slot) — that noise alone was enough to blow past the trait's
threshold of 8, maxing variety for almost everyone regardless of their
actual pattern. Combined with sociability commonly scoring high too in a
small team, (variety, social) — exactly The Chameleon — dominated nearly
every profile. Start times are now bucketed to the nearest half hour before
counting, so the trait measures genuinely different shift patterns instead
of minute-level entry noise.

entries.summary: On This Day weekday matching + crew, three Bingo fixes, all-time board
entries.details:
On This Day:
- Added a "same weekday" match mode alongside the existing exact-date one,
  so last year's Saturday can line up with this year's Saturday instead of
  whatever day the literal anniversary date falls on. Exact date stays the
  default since milestones (birthdays, anniversaries) are calendar events.
- This year's shift(s) now show who you're working with, matching the
  flashback cards.

Bingo — three more impossible/repetitive squares fixed:
- "A shift with nobody else on" can't happen (minimum staffing is 2) —
  replaced with "A shift with just one other colleague".
- "Took every break in full" flipped to "Skipped every break this week",
  a proper opposite of the existing "Skipped a break" square.
- "20+ miles of commuting" replaced with "Didn't drive to work at least
  once" (a shift with no miles logged).
- Added an all-time Overall Board: every square in the pool tallied
  against every completed week of history, not just the 24 that get
  dealt onto any one week's card.

entries.summary: Just Finishing Up trophy, fix Pay Forecast's sliding year picker
entries.details:
- Added Just Finishing Up (mirrors Keen Bean) — clock-outs 10+ minutes
  after shift end, alongside the existing Sees It Through.
- Pay Forecast's tax-year dropdown was built as "current selection minus
  0/1/2 years", so picking an older year slid the newer ones out of the
  list entirely — there was no way back to this year. It's now a fixed
  range from the current tax year down to whichever one employment
  started in, so it never shifts and never goes earlier than that.

entries.summary: Update remaining 8pm closing-time checks to 7pm
entries.details:
Bingo, Shift Briefing, Head to Head and Year in Numbers still compared
finish/closing times against the old 20:00 store closing time. The store
has closed at 19:15 on weekdays since 2026-02-01 (already handled in
teamcalendar.js), so these now use 19:00 too, matching the Night Owl
trophy fix from the last commit.

entries.summary: Rework Trophy Cabinet thresholds and add platinum rollover
entries.details:
Several trophies were unwinnable against real store data: Knows Everyone/
Whole Store/Full Crew assumed a bigger team than the ~12 people here, Long
Haul and Night Owl used thresholds no longer reachable now the store closes
at 19:15, and Funding the Nation's top tier (£10k) was wildly unrealistic.
Time Donated could also show a value that looked like it had cleared a tier
it hadn't, because display rounding rounded up past the threshold.

- Removed Knows Everyone / Whole Store / Full Crew; replaced with a
  monthly-resetting Most Colleagues on a Shift trophy.
- Long Haul now tracks the longest shift each month (resets on the 1st)
  with a realistic 5-8h range instead of an impossible lifetime 6-9h.
- Night Owl's late-finish cutoff moved from 20:00 to 19:00.
- Funding the Nation's top tier dropped from £10,000 to £1,000.
- Added No Time to Stop (opposite of Break Taker) and Sees It Through
  (Never Late, but for clocking out) as two new trophies.
- Display values now floor instead of round, so a card can no longer show
  a number that looks like it's already cleared a medal it hasn't.
- Families without a hard physical ceiling now roll over past platinum
  into Platinum ×2, ×3, etc. instead of just sitting "maxed out" forever.

entries.summary: Back-to-hub button on every V3 page, fix browser back/forward
entries.details:
Every V3 feature page now has a back-to-hub link at the top, plus the
router now listens for hashchange so browser Back/Forward actually
updates the visible view instead of just the URL.

entries.summary: Stop treating weekends as non-working days for leave
entries.details:
Reported from the Shifts view: a Saturday and Sunday on booked leave showed
"not a working day — no hours deducted" instead of paid hours. Correct diagnosis
from the user: Screwfix trades 7 days a week, so there is no such thing as a
non-working weekend here.

The leave-hours-per-day maths only ever spread a leave entry's total hours
across its Mon-Fri days, then explicitly zeroed out Sat/Sun. A leave entry
landing entirely on a weekend divided its hours across zero days and vanished
outright; one spanning a weekend gave the weekday portion the whole entry's
hours (overstating them) while the weekend portion got nothing.

Fixed in public/js/shifts.js: every calendar day the leave entry covers now
gets an equal share of the entered hours, weekend included. The "not a working
day" case no longer exists, so the message and the dead branch are gone.

Same bug, in code I wrote three commits ago: v3/overtime.js's leaveHoursByWeek
filtered to Mon-Fri before spreading leave hours across a week, for the exact
same reason — weekend-only leave contributed nothing towards that week's
target, which is what "leave doesn't count towards falling short" was supposed
to fix in the first place. Corrected to match.

Verified with a fixture matching the reported shape — Friday worked, Saturday
and Sunday booked as leave in the same week: pre-fix the weekend leave
contributed 0h and the week could still read as short; now the full 14.8h is
picked up, the week's target drops to 5.2h, and 8h worked against it correctly
reads as over rather than under. Confirmed live in the browser too, and swept
every other view for regressions.

Flagged, not changed: three older places (public/js/shifts.js's month-level
"Contracted this month" figure, and two spots in server.js used by Monthly
Reports and the on-contract Streak) still prorate monthly contracted hours
using a Mon-Fri/5 divisor rather than the 7-day week this business actually
runs. v3/balance.js already handles this correctly by prorating over 7 days.
This is a real inconsistency but changes numbers already relied on in Reports
and Streaks, so it needs a decision rather than a silent change — surfacing it
separately rather than folding it into this fix.

entries.summary: Overtime — count leave towards contract, headline the real extra hours
entries.details:
Reported as "+3.9h beyond contract when I did more than that in one week", with
the body text underneath admitting 48.5h over. Two separate faults.

1. The headline netted extra against short
   It showed extra minus short — 48.5h over and 44.6h short became "+3.9h".
   Those are two different facts about a year and shouldn't cancel out: working
   48 hours beyond contract and taking a fortnight's holiday are both true, and
   the netted figure describes neither. The headline is now the extra hours;
   short and net are tiles beside it for anyone who wants them.

2. Annual leave counted as failing to hit your contract
   The real cause of the huge short weeks. Leave hours count towards your
   contract for that week — a booked day off is a day you were paid for, not a
   day you came up short. Without that, a fortnight's holiday landed as two
   weeks at -20h, and Christmas and Easter weeks looked like slacking.

   Leave is now apportioned across the weekdays each entry covers and taken off
   that week's target. Expressed that way round rather than adding leave to
   hours worked because it behaves correctly when a week of leave (5 × 7.4h) is
   worth more than a 20h contract — adding it would report a week off as 17h of
   overtime. The two are otherwise the same arithmetic.

   Weeks entirely covered by leave are shown greyed with a 🏖️ marker and left
   out of the totals; weeks with part of the week booked off show their target
   as "20h − 7.4h leave" so the adjustment is visible rather than magic.

   A week where leave was booked but shifts were worked anyway — cancelled
   holiday, covering a shift — still counts in full. Caught while checking the
   rendered table: a week with 4 shifts and 27h was being written off because
   the write-off tested the target alone and not whether anything was worked.

Only leave booked in the app can be allowed for, and the view now says so: a
genuinely quiet week with no leave entry still reads as short.

Verified with a fixture reproducing the reported shape — six weeks at +5h plus
a booked fortnight — which pre-fix gave extra=30h, short=40h, net=-10h and now
gives 30h extra, 0h short, two weeks excluded. Plus the part-leave and
worked-through-leave cases.

entries.summary: Collapse the V3 sidebar group to a single button to the hub
entries.details:
The V3 group listed all nineteen entries in the sidebar, which overflowed the
nav container — only the first ten or so were ever visible, and the rest sat
below the fold. The previous release added a fade to hint at the scroll, but
hinting at a problem is not fixing it.

Replaced the whole group with one ✨ V3.0 Features link straight to the hub
page, which already lists everything as grouped, searchable cards. Shorter,
and the features are actually findable now.

  * The V3 link stays highlighted while you are inside any V3 feature, so the
    sidebar still shows where you are and gives you the way back — without it,
    nothing would have been active on eighteen of the views.
  * Every view remains registered, routable and hash-linkable; only the nav
    entries went. Bookmarks and #hash URLs still work.

The nav no longer overflows at all on a normal desktop window (was 200px over).
The footer fade stays, since it still earns its place when every group is
expanded.

Verified: one V3 nav entry, group gone, all 19 views still render clean, the
highlight appears inside features and not elsewhere, and on mobile the button is
reachable and lands on the hub with all 18 cards.

entries.summary: Tick every Money Clock total, and make all 18 features findable
entries.details:
Money Clock
-----------
Only the hero counter moved; every other figure sat still while you earned.
Worse, they disagreed: the server counts an in-progress shift at its FULL value,
so the hero could say £19 earned so far while "today" already claimed the whole
£60.

Now every total that contains the running shift counts it pro-rata and ticks
with it — today, this week, this month, this year, lifetime earned, lifetime
hours, average per shift, and earned-since-last-payday. The first paint uses the
same pro-rata figure, so nothing jumps when the first tick lands.

Two of them move slowly by nature and that is correct, not stuck: lifetime hours
only changes the second decimal every ~36 seconds, and average-per-shift is
divided across 300-plus shifts.

Verified mid-shift that all nine figures advance, that today's total never reads
below the hero, and that today <= week <= month <= year <= lifetime holds while
ticking.

Finding the features
--------------------
Reported as "I can only see 10 features". All 18 were wired correctly — the
sidebar was the problem. With the group open the nav overflows its container by
about 200px, so everything past the first handful sits below the fold with
nothing to suggest it exists.

  * New ✨ All V3 Features hub, first item in the group: every feature as a
    clickable card, grouped into Money / Stats / Day to day / For fun, with a
    search box. Driven by /api/v3/features — which until now nothing consumed —
    so it cannot drift from what actually exists, and any feature this page has
    not been told how to group still appears under "Also here" rather than
    silently vanishing.
  * The sidebar footer now carries a small gradient fade, so a scrollable nav
    reads as having more below it.

Verified: 18 cards, 4 groups, cards navigate, search filters, all 19 views
render clean in both themes at desktop and mobile with no overflow.

entries.summary: Six new V3 features, and version-stamped asset cache busting
entries.details:
Six more views, taking V3 from twelve to eighteen. As with the rest, everything
is derived from data the app already holds — no new inputs.

  🎒 Shift Briefing    the night-before view. Your next shift on one card: who
                       is rostered with you and for how long, what it pays, the
                       turnaround since your last shift, whether it is a
                       delivery day or bank holiday, and how that exact slot has
                       usually gone (typical clock-in, how often you skip the
                       break on it). Flags clopenings and lone shifts up front.
  ⏰ Overtime Tracker  hours above or below contract per ISO week, measured
                       against the contract in force that week so a contract
                       change mid-year is handled. Headline is the share of your
                       pay that comes from beyond-contract hours. Part-worked
                       current weeks are excluded from every average rather than
                       dragging them down.
  📈 Pay Rise History  every rate change with its percentage, weekly value, and
                       the gap since the previous one, plus how each sat against
                       the National Living Wage — a rise that only tracks the
                       legal minimum is not really a rise. Flags when it has
                       been unusually long since the last one, and totals what
                       the rises have earned you versus your original rate.
  🥊 Head to Head      your rota against one colleague's across eight comparable
                       measures, plus shared shifts and hours together. Hours
                       are rostered spans on both sides so it is like for like.
                       Pay is deliberately not compared.
  📊 Year in Numbers   every year side by side with year-on-year change. The
                       current year is flagged partial and compared on its
                       projection, since judging a part-year against a full one
                       is worse than not comparing at all.
  💡 Did You Know      oddities the other views will never surface: days of the
                       week you have never worked, colleagues you have only ever
                       shared one weekday with, mileage in laps of the M25.

Asset cache busting
-------------------
index.html is now served with the running app version stamped into every ?v=
token, instead of hand-maintained date strings.

Those tokens were a standing trap, and it caught me three times building this:
change a JS file, forget to bump its token, and the browser serves last week's
script against a changed API. It fails as "X is not a function" with new HTML
and old JS — confusing precisely because the deploy looks fine. Deriving the
token from package.json means the existing version bump busts every asset
automatically. Cost is one re-download per deploy.

Docs
----
README covers the six new views and their endpoints.

Verified: all 18 endpoints return 200 with sane figures on seeded data,
head-to-head rejects a missing (400) and unknown (404) colleague, and all 18
views render with no console errors in light and dark mode at desktop and
mobile widths with no horizontal overflow. Both regression fixtures still pass.

entries.summary: Remove dead code and duplication in the V3 module
entries.details:
Audited the V3 module with a script that parses the actual sources rather than
by eye (unused exports, unused imports, duplicated fetching, orphaned files,
client/server/HTML wiring mismatches, cache-token drift).

Duplication
  countdowns.js carried its own copy of the gov.uk bank-holiday fetcher —
  written before v3/bankHolidays.js existed and never removed when it did. The
  duplicate was strictly worse: in-memory only, so every container restart
  re-fetched, and no fallback if gov.uk was unreachable. Deleted (~40 lines) in
  favour of the shared module, which persists its cache in settings.

Query efficiency
  on-this-day ran three queries per flashback, and called db.prepare inside the
  map, so identical SQL was re-prepared on every iteration and better-sqlite3's
  statement cache never got a look in. Now three queries total, using an
  IN (...) over the matched dates.

Dead code removed
  - isBankHolidayShift(): written for stats.js, which ended up inlining the same
    check. Never called from anywhere.
  - DOW_SHORT in helpers.js: never used.
  - Unused exports on bingo/breakDebt/forecast/trophies/stats/leaveYear and
    helpers (pad, rateRecordForDate). The functions are still used internally;
    only the export surface shrank, so nothing changes at runtime.
  - Unused `db` import in records.js.

Checked and found clean: no orphaned files server-side or client-side, every
client view has a matching FEATURES entry, view div and nav link, and all V3
assets share one cache token.

No behaviour change. Verified with the full endpoint sweep plus both regression
fixtures (trophy/record fixes and the payday/leave fixes) — all still pass.

entries.summary: Shift DNA for colleagues, rename The Floater, explain Work-Life Balance
entries.details:
Shift DNA
---------
Now profiles anyone, not just you. A person dropdown lists every colleague with
at least five shifts on record (below that the traits are noise), and the whole
view re-scores against their rota.

One difference is deliberately surfaced rather than hidden: colleague_shifts
carries no break information, so colleague hours are the full rostered span
while yours are paid hours. That makes Endurance read slightly high for
colleagues, and the view says so instead of quietly comparing unlike numbers.

Sociability for a colleague counts everyone else on at the same time, including
you — you are part of their shop floor too.

Renamed "The Floater", which read as an insult rather than a description, to
"The Chameleon" (fits into any shift with anyone). Added two more archetypes so
strong trait pairs are less likely to fall through to The All-Rounder: The
Marathon (weekend + endurance) and The Machine (consistency + endurance).
Copy throughout is no longer second-person, since it may be describing someone
else.

Work-Life Balance
-----------------
Added a "What this score actually measures" card, because the number meant
nothing on its own. It states the one question the score asks — how much genuine
recovery time the rota left — and gives a table of all five measures with what
each looks at, what scores full marks, what scores zero, and its weight. The
verdict bands are shown with the current one highlighted. All of it is driven by
the same constants that compute the score, so the explanation cannot drift from
the maths.

Ranges now go well beyond a year: 4/8/12 weeks, 6 months, 1/2/3 years and all
time (back to your first shift). Past six months the trend chart groups by month
rather than week — a bar per week over three years is an unreadable comb — and
compares against the contracted hours scaled to the length of each month.

entries.summary: Tiered trophies, fix unreachable/miscounted ones, expandable records
entries.details:
Trophy Cabinet
--------------
Every trophy is now a family with four tiers (bronze/silver/gold/platinum)
instead of a one-shot award, so there is always a next target: 22 trophies,
88 medals, up from 31 flat awards. Progress bars measure position within the
current tier band, not distance to platinum.

Three reported bugs, all real:

  * "Work 3 bank holidays" showed unearned despite bank holidays being worked.
    It trusted shifts.is_bank_holiday, which is only filled in on some paths
    (manual tick, recalc, Rotageek sync) — plenty of genuinely worked bank
    holidays sit in the table with the flag still 0. Now cross-references the
    real gov.uk calendar as well as the flag, via a new v3/bankHolidays.js that
    caches the list in settings so it survives restarts and works offline.

  * "The Long Haul" needed 9 paid hours, which nobody on this rota can reach —
    an 8.5h shift minus a 30 minute break is 8 paid hours. That is not a hard
    trophy, it is an impossible one. Retiered to 6/7/8/9 so the top tier is a
    stretch rather than a fiction.

  * "The Whole Store" was a fixed 25 colleagues. Now a percentage of the team
    that actually exists (colleagues without a left_date), so a new starter
    genuinely puts it back out of reach until you have worked with them too.
    Already-earned medals are kept.

New clock-based trophies, since clock_entries was going unused: Keen Bean
(clock-ins 10+ minutes early) and Time Donated (cumulative early minutes).

The hero's tier tallies were unreadable — bronze/silver/gold text sat on the
orange gradient at almost no contrast. They now have their own tile strip on
the normal card background.

Record Book
-----------
  * "Longest run of days worked" undercounted: it filtered on completed = 1, so
    an unticked shift in the middle split one run into two. A genuine 9-day run
    with two unticked days reported 6. Now counts every logged shift up to
    today, ticked or not. Same fix applied across all career stats.

  * Ties are no longer hidden. A 7.5h shift is not rare, and naming one date as
    the record holder implied it was. Records now carry every entry sharing the
    best score, shown as a ×N badge that expands to the full list.

  * New clock records, which the rota alone cannot answer: longest actual time
    on site (clock-in to clock-out, which can beat the scheduled shift),
    earliest clock-in, keenest and latest clock-in, and cumulative early/late
    time. Records are now grouped into shifts / clock / spans / people.

Also bumps the ?v= cache tokens on every changed V3 asset. Without that,
browsers hold the previous JS for a week against a changed API shape — which
is exactly what happened in local testing before the bump.

Verified with a fixture reproducing each reported symptom: a 9-day run with
unticked days in the middle, four bank holidays with the flag unset, 8h as the
longest possible shift, a 13-way tie, and a colleague joining mid-test.

entries.summary: Fix payday accrual window and leave remaining; clarify Pay Forecast
entries.details:
Two V3 bugs reported from the deployed app, plus a fair complaint that the Pay
Forecast was hard to read.

1. Money Clock — "Earned since" showed £0.00 from the wrong date

   The last payday was derived by stepping back a single day from the next one
   and taking that month's payday. Whenever payday falls late in the month, one
   day back is still the same month, so it returned the NEXT payday as the
   previous one — an empty window, hence £0.00 and a nonsensical future date.

   Now steps back a whole month, and counts from the day after that payday so a
   shift can never fall in two pay periods. The card names the last payday, the
   date counting starts, and how many shifts are in the window, and says plainly
   that payroll cut-off means this is a guide rather than what the payslip says.

2. Countdown Board — "Entitlement fully used" with 4h actually remaining

   The countdown had reimplemented leave from scratch and got three things wrong
   that the Leave view gets right: entitlement is per leave year and in HOURS
   (`leave_hours_<year>`), not the global `annual_leave_entitlement` in days;
   only 'annual' leave counts against it, so sick leave was wrongly eating the
   balance; and the year window was "365 days back" rather than the configured
   leave-year boundary.

   Replaced with v3/leaveYear.js, a deliberate mirror of public/js/leave.js so
   the two cannot disagree, documented as such. An unset entitlement now reads
   "no entitlement set" instead of the actively misleading "fully used".

3. Pay Forecast — made the uncertainty legible

   The forecast fills the weeks after your rota ends with an assumption, and
   that assumption was contracted hours only. For a 20h contract with regular
   extra shifts that understates badly — on test data, £15,700 vs £19,211 gross.
   It was also invisible: one big number with no sense of how much was fact.

   - the basis is now switchable between contracted hours and your actual
     average over the last 12 weeks, showing what the other choice implies
   - the hero states how much of the total is already banked or worked, how much
     is booked on the rota, and how much is genuinely estimated
   - "still to pay" relabelled "not yet deducted", with a note that tax is
     computed on the annual figure and that real PAYE self-corrects monthly —
     it was reading as a bill

Verified against the reported scenario (21 Aug 2026, payslips on the 29th, leave
year from 01-01, 4h remaining): the accrual window now starts 30/07 and its total
matches a direct DB sum, and leave reports 4h, with sick leave and the prior
leave year correctly excluded. Full sweep of all 12 views clean in both themes at
desktop and mobile, no overflow, no console errors.

entries.summary: Fix container crash loop — Dockerfile never copied v3/
entries.details:
The V3.0 release crash-looped on deploy with:

    Error: Cannot find module './v3'
    at Object.<anonymous> (/app/server.js:22:18)

`COPY *.js ./` matches top-level files in the build context only — it does not
recurse into subdirectories. Every server-side module before now happened to live
at the repo root, so the glob had always been sufficient by accident. v3/ is the
first server code in a subdirectory, so it was silently left out of the image
while server.js still required it, killing the container on startup.

The client-side half was unaffected: `COPY public/ ./public/` copies a directory
recursively, so public/js/v3/ and public/css/v3.css were already in the image.

Adds an explicit `COPY v3/ ./v3/`, matching the Dockerfile's existing style of
naming what goes in, plus a comment on the non-recursive glob so the next
subdirectory does not repeat this.

Verified without Docker by parsing the Dockerfile's COPY instructions and
replaying them into a staging directory using Docker's own semantics, then
booting the real server.js from that tree. Against the previous Dockerfile this
reproduces the exact production error; against this one the server starts and
serves all 12 features and 31 trophies, with all 14 v3/ modules present.

entries.summary: Add V3.0 Features — 12 new views in a self-contained module
entries.details:
Adds an "✨ V3.0 Features" section to the sidebar with twelve new views. All of
them are new lenses on data the app already holds; only the Goal Tracker asks for
any new input, and nothing here modifies an existing shift, payslip or colleague.

  💸 Money Clock       live earnings ticker for the shift you are on, plus
                       today/week/month/year/lifetime totals and a payday
                       countdown inferred from real payslip payment dates
  ⏳ Countdown Board   next shift, home time, day off, payday, leave, bank
                       holiday, birthdays and work anniversary, ticking live
  🎯 Goal Tracker      money/hours/shifts targets with projected finish dates
                       and whether the booked rota already covers the gap
  🔮 Pay Forecast      tax-year projection of gross, tax, NI and take-home,
                       built from banked payslips -> worked -> booked -> estimated
  🏆 Trophy Cabinet    31 achievements across four rarity tiers
  📖 Record Book       personal bests and lifetime totals
  🧬 Shift DNA         six traits scored from your rota, resolved to an archetype
  ⚖️ Work-Life Balance 0-100 sustainability score over the last N weeks
  ☕ Break Debt        unpaid break minutes, priced, with a better/worse trend
  ⛽ Commute Cost      fuel/wear/parking, and minutes per shift worked to cover it
  📼 On This Day       same date in previous years, plus milestones landing today
  🎲 Rota Bingo        a weekly 5x5 card that ticks itself from real shifts

Kept deliberately separable:

  v3/               one router per feature, mounted at /api/v3 by a single
                    app.use in server.js. index.js holds the FEATURES list as
                    the one source of truth; helpers.js and stats.js carry the
                    shared logic; schema.js owns the only two new tables, both
                    prefixed v3_ so they cannot collide with anything existing.
  public/js/v3/     one view per feature. v3core.js provides the V3 namespace,
                    API surface, render helpers and a view registry.
  public/css/v3.css all styles scoped to .v3-*, inheriting the existing CSS
                    custom properties so dark mode works without new rules.

The blast radius on shared files is 3 lines in server.js and 11 in app.js. The
router resolves V3 views through the registry rather than naming them, so a
thirteenth feature needs no change to app.js at all.

Verified end to end against a seeded database: every endpoint returns 200 with
sane figures, goal CRUD and its validation paths behave, the bingo card is
deterministic per week, and all twelve views render with no console errors in
light and dark mode, at desktop and mobile widths, with no horizontal overflow.
Timers in Money Clock and Countdown Board are confirmed to stop on navigate away.

entries.summary: Major cleanup — remove Ollama/LM Studio, dead code, fix DB bloat and a real bug
entries.details:
Removed entirely (decided against local-model OCR — Gemini covers AI screenshot
import instead):
- The whole Ollama/LM Studio job-queue pipeline: background worker, image slicing,
  model-list/pull endpoints, Photo Library "Queue" buttons, and the 8-second global
  badge-polling loop that ran on every page regardless of which view was open.
- The "attach screenshot when completing a shift" option (unused).
- Two broken legacy Tesseract OCR routes — one was calling a function that doesn't
  exist anywhere in the codebase, already silently broken.
- 22 dead api.js wrapper methods, including one pointing at a URL that never existed.
- Orphaned frontend handlers (dead tax-refund modal, dead Rotageek login handlers,
  an "Update token" button that scrolled to a field no longer in the DOM).
- tesseract.js and jimp from package.json (regenerated package-lock.json).

Fixed:
- DB bloat: the orphaned ocr_jobs/ocr_job_files tables held ~234MB of full-resolution
  screenshot blobs that were never cleared after a job finished. A one-time migration
  drops both tables and VACUUMs on next startup to reclaim the space.
- Manage People's "Merge" button called a route that never existed (instant 404) —
  implemented POST /colleagues/:srcId/merge-into/:dstId to match what the UI expected.
- Dashboard/Who's In/Clock In-Out timers now stop when navigating away instead of
  accumulating in the background for the life of the browser tab.

2,315 lines removed, 80 added, across 17 files.

entries.summary: Add search and renamed/unrenamed filter to Photo Library
entries.details:
Search box filters by filename live; a filter dropdown narrows to
renamed-only or not-renamed-only photos, with a shown-count indicator.
Select All now respects the active filter/search instead of always
selecting the whole folder.

entries.summary: Add Select All to Photo Library
entries.details:
A "Select All" button now sits above the photo grid, always visible (unlike
the bulk-action toolbar which only appears once something's selected).
Toggles to "Deselect All" once everything's picked, kept in sync with
individual photo selection.

entries.summary: Fix Photo Library auto-rename checkbox layout, move What If? into V2.0 Features
entries.details:
The auto-rename checkbox used ad-hoc inline styles that got clobbered by the
global "input { width: 100% }" rule, stretching the checkbox across the row
and splitting it from its label text. Switched to the app's existing
.toggle-label pattern (already used for payslip form toggles) instead.

What If? moved from Pay & Stats into V2.0 Features, alongside Synergy Score,
Team Metrics, Fatigue Audit, Shift Heatmap, and Weather.

entries.summary: Photo Library week auto-save/rename, upload-time auto-rename, remove Compare Sources
entries.details:
Team Upload's Auto Import (AI) now saves a copy of each screenshot into a
"Team Rota Screenshots" folder, named from the same week range Gemini already
extracts (DD.MM.YYYY - DD.MM.YYYY) - no extra AI calls needed. Photo Library
gained an "AI Rename" bulk action for photos already there, and an
"auto-rename with AI on upload" checkbox that reads and renames screenshots
at upload time without importing any shifts - both share the same rename
logic. Added a week_start_date column for correct chronological sorting,
since a DD.MM.YYYY filename doesn't sort correctly as plain text.

Removed Compare Sources (nav entry, view, route, API method) - unused and no
longer needed now that import conflicts are resolved properly at import time.

entries.summary: Automatic Gemini model fallback on overload, with capability ranking surfaced in Settings
entries.details:
callGeminiVision() now tries the configured model first; on an "overloaded/high
demand" error it fetches the live list of models available to the key (same
source as the existing Settings refresh button, so nothing is hardcoded and
can't go stale the way a fixed model name did before), ranks them by
capability, and retries with up to 3 of the best alternatives before giving
up. Applies to both team screenshot import and payslip photo import. Callers
now surface which model actually produced a result, and the frontend notes it
in the status message whenever a fallback was used instead of the configured
model.

The same ranking now orders GET /colleagues/gemini-models and is surfaced in
Settings — the top-ranked model is marked "Recommended (most capable)" and
auto-selected on refresh, so picking a strong model isn't guesswork.

entries.summary: Real same-day overwrite/keep-both choice for team shift import conflicts
entries.details:
/colleagues/import-json only flagged a conflict when the incoming shift's start
time exactly matched an existing one for that colleague+date — a same-day shift
with a different start time (e.g. a misread of an already-imported shift)
silently inserted as a brand-new row instead of prompting. The other import
paths (OCR/Ollama) already used the broader detectConflicts() same-day check;
this route now matches that behaviour.

Each conflict now lists every existing shift that colleague has that day and
lets you choose per-row: skip (default), replace one specific existing shift
with the incoming one, or keep both as separate shifts (genuine split shift).

entries.summary: Add Undo Last Import for team shift imports
entries.details:
Every colleague-shift import path (screenshot OCR, Gemini, Ollama/LM Studio via
the job queue, JSON paste/AI extract, bulk API) now opens an import_batches
record and tags each row it inserts with that batch id. Team Upload shows a
"Recent Imports" panel listing the last several imports with an Undo button
that deletes only the rows still belonging to that batch — never touches
data that existed before the import or was added by something else.

Overridden conflicts (an existing row updated rather than a new one inserted)
are deliberately left untagged, since undoing should never delete data that
predates the import.

entries.summary: Support multiple screenshots in AI Team Upload import
entries.details:
The Auto Import (AI) drop zone only accepted one screenshot at a time.
Now accepts multiple files (drop or picker), reads each with Gemini in
sequence with per-file progress status, and feeds all results into the
existing multi-file preview/import pipeline together.
